critical_findings.finding: Evidence pointer objects are not consistently using the required canonical structure {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}. The decision_log uses evidence_pointers containing extra/nonstandard fields (e.g., candidate_id, artifact_id, quote), which risks validator failure under R10 and breaks the “single evidence standard” contract for downstream consumers.

closure.closure_target: Standardize evidence pointer schema across all artifacts and enforce via a single linter/validator; migrate decision_log evidence_pointers to the R10 structure (or add a separate, explicitly non-evidence field for ancillary metadata).

critical_findings.finding: Tool policy for the Review stage denies artifact_write and workspace_write, but the workflow requires reviewers to emit review_findings.json as a deliverable. This creates an unresolvable contract conflict (review can’t produce its required canonical output under its own permissions), risking deadlock or ad-hoc bypasses that undermine determinism and governance.

closure.closure_target: Revise Review stage policy to allow writing a tightly-scoped findings artifact only (e.g., artifact_write=allow_canonical_review_findings_only), while still enforcing “findings-only” (no patch/code outputs). Add an explicit validator that reviewer outputs are limited to review_findings.json schema.

critical_findings.finding: Stage model is internally inconsistent: requirements define minimum stages (Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze), but tool policy includes PatchApply and IntegrateAndValidate stages, and milestones include a Patch & Repair phase. This mismatch risks missing required stage_handoffs, incorrect gate enforcement, or orchestrator rejecting the plan as not matching the declared state machine.

closure.closure_target: Make a single canonical stage taxonomy and apply it consistently across: R4/AT4, tool_policy.stage_policies, milestones, and architecture dataflow. Ensure every transition has an enforced stage_handoff requirement and acceptance test coverage.

critical_findings.finding: Secrets handling requirement (“never store secrets in logs/workspace; block persistence”) can conflict with append-only event_log immutability if secrets are detected after a write. Without an explicit “pre-write scan gate” design, the system can end up either violating append-only constraints (by mutating/deleting log entries) or violating secrets policy (by persisting secrets even briefly).

closure.closure_target: Define an explicit write-path: (1) pre-persistence secrets_scan must pass for any artifact/event payload; (2) if post-facto detection occurs, append a redaction/incident record and rotate/rekey pointers while preserving immutability (no deletion). Add validator tests ensuring no secret-bearing bytes are ever committed to canonical storage.

critical_findings.finding: artifact_ref format is explicitly an unresolved blocking open question, yet it is foundational to evidence pointers and workspace_index entries. Without a fixed artifact_ref naming/versioning/addressing spec, evidence pointers cannot be guaranteed to resolve deterministically, undermining trace completeness gates and downstream reproducibility.

closure.closure_target: Resolve Q3 by defining artifact_ref as a typed, versioned identifier with validation rules (e.g., regex + immutable content-hash binding) and include it in schemas for evidence pointers and workspace_index. Add a pointer-resolution validator that fails on any non-resolving reference.

critical_findings.finding: Deterministic retry/quarantine policy is required (R23) but key parameters remain unspecified (e.g., retry budgets/backoff and how retries are recorded), and are marked as blocking open questions. This risks non-deterministic gate outcomes, inconsistent freeze decisions, or budget-exhaustion deadlocks.

closure.closure_target: Specify exact deterministic retry algorithm (max retries per validator per stage, fixed backoff schedule, flaky classification thresholds, quarantine rules) and a strict event_log schema for recording each attempt. Add acceptance tests that assert identical outcomes across replays given the same inputs.

critical_findings.finding: Big-bang, fully sequential flow with high HITL strictness increases the likelihood of context-pack growth and wall-clock delays, but the plan does not define concrete bounded context-pack selection/eviction rules beyond high-level intent. This can cause either overflow (truncation-driven errors) or under-selection (missing critical artifacts), especially late in the pipeline.

closure.closure_target: Define and version explicit context-pack policies: required-minimum artifact sets per stage/role, deterministic prioritization order, byte/token ceilings, and a validator that checks both completeness and bounds. Consider adding a “context adequacy” gate before Judge.

critical_findings.finding: The “smallest passing repair” deterministic selection rule may systematically choose a patch that passes current gates but increases long-term risk (maintainability/security posture) because selection criteria are limited to ops/bytes/first-generated. The plan acknowledges this risk (K21) but does not define a deterministic secondary scoring/gating mechanism.

closure.closure_target: Add deterministic secondary evaluators (e.g., lint/style deltas, complexity delta thresholds, security scan delta) as additional pass/fail validators or deterministic scoring inputs, with an explicit HITL trigger when candidates differ materially on these signals.
